title: Folders and file names
hook: List a card dump, count clips by type and rename them all in one go.

warmup.q: A file already has text in it. You open it with mode `"w"` and write one line. What is left?
options: The old text plus your line
warmup.explain: `"w"` erases first, then writes. To keep the old text and add to it, use `"a"`.

options: Brings in a ready-made toolbox of code
warmup.explain: A module is code someone else wrote. `import` lets you use it, like `random` or `math`.
`split` cuts the text at every `_` and gives a list of the pieces.

why.heading: Why folders
why.text: A card dump is 200 files named like `A001_C003.mp4`. Renaming by hand takes an hour and you will slip. Python can list a folder, pick out the video files and rename every one in a blink. The tool for it is **pathlib**.

why.heading: A Path is an address
why.text: `from pathlib import Path` brings in one tool from the module. Then `Path("clips")` is a folder address and `Path("clips/A001_C003.mp4")` is a file address. It is only an address, nothing is opened yet.

why.heading: Parts of a name
why.text:
An address knows its pieces. For `p = Path("clips/A001_C003.mp4")`:

`p.name` is `A001_C003.mp4`
`p.stem` is `A001_C003`
`p.suffix` is `.mp4`

The **suffix** is the file type. The **stem** is the name without it.

why.heading: Join and look
why.text: Join with `/`: `Path("clips") / "notes.txt"`. Ask `.exists()` for True or False. `folder.glob("*.mp4")` finds every match, where `*` means anything. Wrap it as `sorted(folder.glob("*.mp4"))` so the order is always the same. `folder.iterdir()` lists everything.

why.heading: Rename
why.text: `p.rename(new_path)` renames the file on disk. It is real and there is no undo, so practise on copies. Build the new address from the folder: `p.rename(folder / "new.mp4")`. Never rename while you are mid-way through a loop over the live folder: make the list first with `sorted(...)`.

watch.intro: Tap Run. A small fake folder called clips holds two videos and a text file. Python lists only the videos.
watch.code:
from pathlib import Path
folder = Path("clips")
for p in sorted(folder.glob("*.mp4")):
    print(p.name, p.stem, p.suffix)
print(folder.exists(), (folder / "missing.txt").exists())
explain: `glob("*.mp4")` matches only names ending in .mp4, so notes.txt is skipped.
`sorted(...)` puts them in the same order every time.
For each clip we print its name, its stem (no type) and its suffix (the type).
The last line asks if the folder exists (True) and if missing.txt exists (False).
watch.break_it: Change `"*.mp4"` to `"*.mov"` and tap Run. There is no error, the loop just finds nothing, so only `True False` shows. A glob that matches nothing is silent. Put it back.

tasks.title: List the clips
tasks.task:
The folder `day1` has some video files and a log. Show only the file names of the `.mp4` files, one per line. The result for the first test is:

`A001_C001.mp4`
`A001_C002.mp4`
tasks.starter:
from pathlib import Path
folder = Path("day1")
for p in sorted(folder.glob("*.mp4")):
    print(p)
tasks.solution:
from pathlib import Path
folder = Path("day1")
for p in sorted(folder.glob("*.mp4")):
    print(p.name)
hints: Printing `p` shows the whole address, with the folder. You only want one part of it.
The part with the name and type together is `p.name`.

tasks.title: Count by type
tasks.task:
The folder `card` has video and sound files. Count them by type and show:

`MP4: 3`
`WAV: 1`

(for the first test files). Use `.suffix` to tell them apart.
tasks.starter:
from pathlib import Path
mp4 = 0
wav = 0
for p in sorted(Path("card").iterdir()):
    # count by p.suffix here
    pass
print("MP4:", mp4)
print("WAV:", wav)
hints: Inside the loop, `p.suffix` is a string like `.mp4`. Compare it with `==`.
Use if p.suffix == ".mp4": then add 1 to mp4. Use elif for the .wav files.
if p.suffix == ".mp4":  then  mp4 += 1   and   elif p.suffix == ".wav":  then  wav += 1

tasks.title: Add a prefix to every clip
tasks.task:
The folder `raw` has some `.mp4` clips. Rename each one by adding `ICL_` at the front, so `A001.mp4` becomes `ICL_A001.mp4`. At the end show how many you renamed, like:

`Renamed 2`
tasks.starter:
from pathlib import Path
folder = Path("raw")
n = 0
for p in sorted(folder.glob("*.mp4")):
    # rename p here
    n += 1
print("Renamed", n)
tasks.solution:
from pathlib import Path
folder = Path("raw")
n = 0
for p in sorted(folder.glob("*.mp4")):
    p.rename(folder / ("ICL_" + p.name))
    n += 1
print("Renamed", n)
hints: `p.rename(...)` needs the new address inside the brackets.
The new address is the folder, joined with / to the new name. The new name is "ICL_" plus p.name.

recap: `from pathlib import Path` gives you addresses: `Path("clips")`.
`.name` is the full file name, `.stem` is without the type, `.suffix` is the type.
`/` joins a folder and a name. `.exists()` is True or False.
`sorted(folder.glob("*.mp4"))` lists matching files in a steady order.

words.meaning: The module for working with folders and file names.
An address of a file or folder. It is not opened until you ask.
The file name without its type: A001_C003.
The file type at the end, with the dot: .mp4
Find files by a pattern. `*` stands for anything.
